results.title: Midterm election results will slow data center buildout, experts predict
results.author: Megan  Cerullo
results.content:
The Democrats' in the midterm elections on Tuesday could buoy opponents of data centers in some parts of the U.S. and slow the spread of the controversial facilities, according to Wall Street analysts.
As of Wednesday afternoon, voters had approved 38 ballot measures restricting data centers in communities across California, Illinois, Maine, Ohio, New York and other states, according to an analysis from political research firm Redbud Consulting. Residents in Harwood, North Dakota, were the only voters to approve a data center.
The election also elevates a number of state and gubernatorial candidates who made stricter regulation of data centers a key part of their campaigns.
The rapid development of data centers around the U.S. to help power artificial intelligence has provoked widespread public backlash. By a margin of more than 2-to-1, more Americans oppose than favor building a new data center in their area, a found this summer.
Focus on Texas
Franklin Templeton chief market strategist Stephen Dover predicted that the election results will lead to a "slowdown in data centers being built," bringing new regulations and costs for their developers.
"For tech investors, the big focus is will these midterm elections slow the pace of the planned 800 to 1,000 data centers across the U.S. fueling the AI Revolution," Yorkville Ives & Co. technology analyst Dan Ives said in a report. "The answer in our view is a clear YES."
Ives pointed to Texas, which accounts for 25% to 30% of the expected to come online by 2030, as one state that could be affected. Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who defeated Republican iin the race for governor, proposed a temporary ban on data center construction during her campaign.
"Texas is the foundation of the AI buildout in the U.S.," Ives told CBS News.
Hinojosa's win over Abbott could stall the addition of 13 gigawatts of data-center power in Texas, according to Gordon Johnson, CEO and founder of the investment adviser GLJ Research.
Abbott had already suspended data center approvals, which makes it easy for Hinojosa to extend the moratorium.
"Texas already has a moratorium — Abbott built it. All the new governor has to do is keep it in place. She doesn't need a new law to keep data center permits frozen," Johnson told CBS News.
Keisha Lance Bottoms' , the third-largest data center market, also has significant implications for the infrastructure buildout.
Bottoms, who campaigned on pausing new data center construction in the state, on Wednesday that she would immediately "sign an executive order for that pause, and then we will determine what else we need to do administratively to take that pause into effect."
Bottoms also said she plans to review tax incentives offered in Georgia that have spurred data center development.
"So, of course, we are going to have to take a look at what those agreements entail and determine what our remedies are to enact that pause, but I don't think we're going to get a lot of pushback across the state," she said. "Many local governments have already taken that first step."
Cooling an overheated sector
Market analyst Adam Crisafulli of Vital Knowledge noted that semiconductor, hardware and other stocks associated with data center construction fell sharply on Wednesday amid investor concerns over permitting delays.
Seema Shah, chief global strategist at Principal Asset Management, thinks data center developers could face additional requirements to invest in electrical grids and potentially lose tax incentives, thereby raising their costs. She added in a research note that higher development costs for new facilities could "increase the value of existing infrastructure that is already powered, permitted, and operational."
Massive investment in data centers and the artificial intelligence sector more broadly has helped propel U.S. economic growth and drive stock market gains. In the long term, however, a slower data center buildout is unlikely to hamstring the economy, Dover of Franklin Templeton told CBS News.
"It's possible to argue that the AI trade and data center buildout was getting overheated, and this could dampen some of the excessive investment that might not have a good return on capital, which investors have questioned anyway," he said. "So unbridled expansion will be tempered a bit, but probably not a lot."
Although data center moratoriums may delay construction, they're unlikely to torpedo capital spending on AI or short-circuit broader growth, according to economists.
"A more restrictive stance toward data centers would stretch the timelines of future projects, and slower construction in the medium to long term wouldn't necessarily be a bad outcome for the macroeconomy," analysts with Oxford Economics said in a report.
results.summary:
Recent midterm election results across the United States have empowered local and state officials to implement stricter regulations and moratoriums on the rapid expansion of new data centers.

### Key Points
- Voters approved 38 ballot measures restricting data center development across states including California, Illinois, Ohio, and New York.
- Texas, which represents up to 30% of planned U.S. data center capacity by 2030, faces potential construction delays following the gubernatorial election.
- Georgia Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms plans to sign an executive order pausing new data center construction and reviewing existing tax incentives.
- Analysts from Yorkville Ives & Co. and GLJ Research suggest these political shifts will likely slow the development of hundreds of planned AI-focused facilities.
- Semiconductor and hardware stocks declined on Wednesday as investors reacted to the prospect of increased permitting costs and regulatory hurdles.

### Why it Matters
The shift toward stricter oversight could increase development costs and extend project timelines for the infrastructure essential to the artificial intelligence industry. While this may temper rapid sector growth, economists suggest it could also prevent market overheating and improve the long-term efficiency of capital investment.

results.title: Dow surges 1,000 points as Democrats take control of Congress
results.author: Max Zahn
results.content:
Dow closes up 1,500 points as Democrats take control of Congress
Stocks soared on Wednesday, just hours after results showed a blue wave.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up more than 1,500 points on Wednesday, just hours after midterm election results showed Democrats had taken control of the U.S. House and Senate.
The S&P 500 finished the trading session up 1.5%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq increased 1.4%.
The Dow jumped 1,570 points, or 3%, recording its best one-day performance since April 9, 2025, when President Donald Trump announced the suspension of a far-reaching set of reciprocal tariffs.
Oil prices, meanwhile, plunged on Wednesday after Vice President JD Vance issued a statement on X blaming the Republican defeats on the Iran war.
The West Texas Intermediate futures price, a benchmark index for U.S. trading, dropped more than 7%, registering at about $88.60 a barrel.
The national average price of a gallon of gas stands at $4.12, marking an increase of $1.14 since the outbreak of the Iran war in February, AAA data showed. Over the past month, the national average has dropped 24 cents a gallon.
"Unless something significant changes, we could be looking at the national average price of gasoline falling below $4/gal in the next week," GasBuddy analyst Patrick De Haan said in a social media post.
A blue wave on Tuesday catapulted Democratic Senate candidates to victories in Republican strongholds such as South Carolina and Texas. As of Wednesday morning, Democrats had won 54 seats in the Senate, with competitive races yet to be called in Alaska and Mississippi.
A strong performance in House contests, meanwhile, appeared to set Democrats on a path toward a comfortable majority in the lower chamber.
Jim Reid, a research strategist at Deutsche Bank, described the midterm results as in line with past examples of a party out of power running against an unpopular president.
"This looks like a perfectly normal election by historical standards. Markets appear to have welcomed that normality, with an emerging relief rally as things stand," Reid said in a memo to clients shared with ABC News.
Jeremy Richardson, a senior portfolio manager for Global Equities at RBC Global Asset Management, voiced similar sentiment about relief among investors.
"Midterm election results were consistent with market expectations and betting market predictions, mitigating the risk of significant short-term price dislocations," Richardson said in a statement to ABC News.
Despite the uptick in stocks, at least one analyst cautioned about the risk for the tech sector posed by newly empowered Democrats, many of whom ran campaigns critical of artificial intelligence data centers.
"The Democratic blue tidal wave across the Senate and House was a seismic shift that will have a negative impact on the pace of the AI Revolution buildout in the US over the next few years," Dan Ives of Yorkville said.
In recent years, stock gains have been propelled in part by a handful of tech giants known as the "Magnificent 7": Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Tesla and Nvidia. Many of those firms have embraced AI.
"There is no way to sugarcoat that Democrats taking control, especially over the Senate, will create some major hurdles for AI and tech legislation," Ives added.
Investors, however, appeared to shrug off that concern -- at least with regard to some tech giants.
Microsoft, which holds a large stake in OpenAI, saw its stock price close up more than 6% in early trading. Amazon, which has spent hundreds of billions on its build out of AI infrastructure, also closed up more than 6%.
By contrast, shares fell for some large tech firms. Nvidia, the giant chipmaker fueling AI products, saw shares close down about 3%.
results.summary:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged over 1,500 points on Wednesday as Democratic victories in the midterm elections secured control of both the U.S. House and Senate.

### Key Points
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 3%, marking its strongest single-day performance since April 9, 2025.
- Democrats secured 54 Senate seats, including key victories in Republican strongholds like Texas and South Carolina.
- West Texas Intermediate oil futures dropped over 7% to $88.60 per barrel following comments from Vice President JD Vance.
- Microsoft and Amazon shares each climbed 6%, while Nvidia stock declined 3% amid concerns over future AI regulation.
- GasBuddy analysts project the national average price of gasoline could fall below $4 per gallon within the next week.

### Why it Matters
The market rally reflects investor relief that the election results aligned with historical norms and pre-election betting market predictions. However, the shift in legislative power introduces potential regulatory headwinds for the artificial intelligence sector and major tech companies that have driven recent market growth.

results.title: The Enterprise Case for Open-Weight Models on Databricks
results.author: Jay Palaniappan, Elise Gonzales, Tanner Waggoner, Toby Messinger, Will Middlebrook
results.content:
As field engineers at Databricks, we spend our days inside enterprise AI deployments, where we’ve observed a clear shift in strategy. After two years of standardizing on single frontier model providers, companies are reevaluating their approach due to seven key pressures:
1. Spend is not generating sufficient returns. AI budgets have outpaced revenue and cost savings, prompting a need for better unit economics [1].
2. Model rankings have changed repeatedly since 2023. The best model for coding, reasoning, and extraction changes month to month, and the top intelligence ranking has changed hands 20+ times since May 2023 [2]. Architectures tied to a single provider make it harder to adopt a better model as rankings change.
3. Frontier guardrails can block legitimate work. Model guardrails imposed by AI labs can refuse legitimate tasks, such as analyzing live malware or reproducing an exploit to patch it, a limitation discovered in the recent Hugging Face incident [6][7]. When Hugging Face responders fed real attack logs and exploit payloads to hosted frontier models for analysis, the guardrails refused, and the team ran the analysis on an open-weight model (GLM 5.2) instead.
4. Data retention policies have evolved and may continue to do so. Some frontier providers have deviated from zero-data-retention (ZDR) policies, such as the 30-day minimum retention introduced with Anthropic's frontier tier [8]. For enterprises whose compliance policy was written around the principle that "no prompt or completion is ever stored," an upstream policy change could introduce problems and potentially require a system change.
5. Companies want visibility into and control over model governance. Demand is growing for end-to-end visibility and governance across AI models. Customers want searchable records of model inputs, outputs, errors, and agent actions to enable teams to evaluate accuracy and improve performance, as well as centralized controls to protect sensitive data and intellectual property.
6. The harness matters as much as the model. Databricks’ research shows that the scaffolding around a model, its harness of prompts, tools, and control flow, changes measured performance. In Databricks’ own benchmark, the same model scored 61.7% in one harness, 48.1% in another, and 38.4% bare [9]. Because harness choice changes benchmark results, evaluations should test the model and harness together.
7. Open-weight models caught up to frontier models. The top open-weight models now benchmark at a level comparable to that of top frontier models at a lower cost [3][4][5]. This was not true eighteen months ago. Open-weight models achieving frontier-level benchmark performance change the cost, control, and deployment trade-offs described in the other six points.
Across these observations, companies are trying to: 1) optimize costs without sacrificing productivity gains, 2) preserve operational freedom, and 3) ensure AI implementations can quickly incorporate innovations. To do so, they need an architecture in which models and harnesses can change without weakening governance.
Open-weight models improve cost efficiency, control, and flexibility over frontier models:
Source: [5] DeepSWE Leaderboard by Cost. Some of the top open-weight models compared against their proprietary equivalents, filtered at the authors’ discretion.
Unity Gateway serves open-weight and frontier models through a unified API with centralized governance controls, enabling teams to switch between models via configuration or smart routing [10][11] rather than through code changes or other abstractions [12][13].
The multi-model capability of Unity Gateway is becoming integral to customers’ AI strategies. Since January, the average number of unique models used per customer has increased from 4.2 to 7.1, an indicator of the options available on Unity Catalog and of the pursuit of higher-ROI models. Of those models, roughly ~40% were open-weight.
Source: Databricks’ internal data from the week ending January 5, 2026, through the week ending July 27, 2026. Created using Genie One.
Serving large open-weight models with competitive response times requires optimization to maintain cost efficiency at scale. Databricks addresses latency constraints by leveraging tailored inference engines and optimized kernels deployed on frontier GPUs. Independent evaluations from Artificial Analysis highlight these performance characteristics: for instance, GLM 5.3 (max) achieves an end-to-end response time (including input processing, reasoning, and generation) of 9.1 seconds on Databricks [15], performing favorably alongside top-tier managed endpoints [16].
Source: [15] GLM 5.3 Model Providers: Artificial Analysis
Here are some key features to help govern these models and control costs on Unity Gateway:
GLM 5.2 coincided with a sharp increase in open-weight usage on Unity Gateway. After GLM 5.2 became available in mid-July, its usage rose. At the same time, growth among Unity Gateway customers remained relatively consistent, suggesting that existing customers shifted more AI traffic toward open-weight models. Just one month after first being offered, GLM 5.2 already accounts for ~40% of open-weight tokens used on Unity Gateway, with most of that growth incremental. Both GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3's benchmark performance give customers another open-weight option to evaluate alongside GLM 5.2 [5].
To support this demand, Databricks announced a $3 billion fundraising round in July, and CEO Ali Ghodsi told CNBC the raise is partially about securing GPU capacity to host open models. "We are running out of GPUs everywhere... Japan, Korea, U.S., and India, so we just needed to get a lot of these, and that requires a lot of funding. So that’s what triggered this fundraiser for us" [22].
The harness your developers already live in can still run open-weight models hosted on Databricks. As of late July, models served on Unity Gateway, including GLM 5.3, can run inside provider coding harnesses such as Codex and OpenCode [12][26], with support for additional harnesses rolling out. The gateway exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints per harness, so the setup is just a config change. Point the harness at your workspace's gateway URL, or use the ucode helper with one line:
ucode codex --model system.ai.glm-5-3
Enterprises should plan for a portfolio of models because no single model or provider will lead in quality, cost, and policy fit for every workload. Of those to choose from, open-weight models now offer competitive intelligence at lower cost and greater control over data handling and governance policies. In contrast, frontier models remain useful where they deliver better results. Unity Gateway manages these options through common access controls, routing policies, budgets, and auditing. Omnigent extends that flexibility to the harness, so teams can change models or agent environments without rebuilding workflows.
The usage data in this article shows that customers are already moving in this direction. They are serving more models, directing more traffic to open weights, and using portable harnesses to broaden their options. The durable advantage is the ability to make those changes quickly as model options, quality, pricing, and policy requirements evolve.

This WTF guide, sponsored by Wurl, explores how CTV advertisers are driving positive attention and improved performance across the entire funnel by aligning creative with relevant onscreen context through scene-level targeting.

Research shows that ad-supported streaming TV services are experiencing a surge in popularity. Despite this boon in both viewership and content supply, CTV advertisers still struggle with an opaque ecosystem that limits the ability to control where their ads appear. On top of this, ad fill rates aren’t quite keeping pace, according to Wurl — signaling a significant opportunity for advertisers and content owners alike. This dynamic is ripe for change, with new tools and technologies now available that promise to help advertisers reach engaged viewers more effectively and efficiently at scale.
Among the new tools is scene-level targeting, a form of contextual advertising that analyzes content on screen just before the ad break to determine which ad should appear next. With scene-level targeting on CTV, advertisers can pinpoint relevant moments for greater impact.
“Effective communication often relies on the context in which it is delivered; the same rules apply in advertising. Scene-level targeting introduces a whole new level of precision to TV advertising,” said Ria Madrid, vice president of global advertising at Wurl. “Marketers can now deliver their brand messaging adjacent to relevant content and in alignment with viewers’ mindsets and level of attentiveness. It creates a smarter, more prescriptive connection between brands and consumers.”
In this WTF explainer guide, Digiday and Wurl examine what scene-level targeting is, how it differs from other targeting strategies and how brands are implementing it.
Scene-level targeting considers what is happening on screen in a show or movie before an ad break — not just the app, channel, genre or audience. By focusing on what is being watched and when — such as the emotional tone or the brand safety of a specific scene — scene-level targeting places ads in compatible moments that feel relevant to viewers.
Advertisers commonly rely solely on audience targeting, which is based on household-level IDs, or on broad, traditional genre targeting that does not account for nuanced moments. But with scene-level signals, brands can better align their creative with the context of a given scene, even if they continue to apply traditional strategies like audience targeting.
Broad targeting treats every scene as equal, when really they aren’t.
“Content isn’t static — tone, emotion and subject matter often shift from one scene to the next. With scene-level analysis and real-time categorization, advertisers now have the ability to respond to that nuance and target accordingly. Scene-level signals introduce precision where it matters most — at the moment of exposure — and bring greater precision to how CTV campaigns are planned and evaluated.” Madrid said.
While more than half of marketers invest in TV and streaming, per Digiday Research, challenges remain in the CTV ad ecosystem. Though CTV investment continues to grow, advertisers still lack consistent, granular signals about content environments. And with the high impact CTV brings — delivering ads on the biggest screen in the home, often in non-skippable environments — context matters even more.
Many moments and scenes within a single TV program can be wildly different. As the show’s narrative progresses, the genre and emotional tone may also change, but program- or channel-level targeting doesn’t capture that nuance.
For instance, the popular series “Succession” was rooted in serious drama, but still delivered moments of sharp, often unexpected humor where an emotionally intense ad would feel out of place. Scene-level targeting aims to avoid that dissonant experience by using a more granular taxonomy to deliver more relevant, timely ads that enhance outcomes for both brands and audiences.
This additional layer of insight supports smarter creative alignment and stronger brand outcomes. According to a joint Wurl and TVision study, there is a 2.4x increase in attention when streaming TV ads match the content’s emotion.
Beyond helping to pinpoint the genre and emotional context, scene-level targeting is also well-suited for addressing brand safety concerns.
Typical channel- and show-level metadata doesn’t catch sensitive, inappropriate or generally misaligned content at the scene level. Because of this limited information, some advertisers entirely avoid potentially problematic content types, like news, to circumvent brand safety issues.
However, Wurl data shows that news accounts for an average of 8.6% of viewing hours on free ad-supported streaming TV, the majority of which is watched by a small but highly engaged segment of viewers — meaning that advertisers that exclude news content from their campaigns are missing out on opportunities to reach a sizable, engaged audience. Furthermore, Wurl’s 2026 CTV trends report found that more than a third of news scenes are fully brand safe. With scene-level targeting, ads can be placed alongside a feel-good news story, rather than a polarizing one, ensuring brand safety while still maximizing reach and message impact.
“Currently, many advertisers are approaching brand safety with overly broad-stroke approaches. Entire genres, programs and sometimes even publishers are excluded in an effort to avoid potential risk,” Madrid said. “By moving beyond broad proxies, advertisers can deliver their ads more intentionally, without sacrificing reach or risk to their brand. For publishers, this unlocks an optimization tool — shifting brand safety from a constraint into a monetization opportunity.”
Scene-level targeting on CTV starts with analyzing content moment by moment and tagging scenes with contextual metadata. It’s worth noting that these solutions don’t rely on cookies, IDs or any data that would run afoul of Video Privacy Protection Act (VPPA) regulations. Those emotional and contextual signals are then used to insert ads into the most relevant, high-impact moments.
For instance, Wurl uses generative AI to analyze video content, evaluating the scene immediately before an ad pod. This proprietary technology scores content across various attributes, including emotions, genres and IAB-defined brand safety categories.
“Our technology analyzes a combination of visual cues, audio signals and dialogue to understand imagery, tone, sentiment and contextual themes as they unfold within a scene,” Madrid said. “By evaluating the combination of these media aesthetics, we advance beyond one-dimensional metadata signals and produce dynamic segment outputs that classify the nuance of what’s happening in the moment. For advertisers, that means stronger alignment and attention. For publishers, it creates high-value, contextually enriched inventory.”
This analysis happens in real time, enabling dynamic and precise ad delivery at scale. As the content is identified and classified, these scores are appended to the content metadata before it is sent to demand-side platforms, where segments can then be targeted. Once these signals are passed into the bid stream, advertisers can choose to target relevant contextual moments that align with their brand.
“Brands have flexibility in how they activate contextual segments for their campaign targeting. They can select on their own from our expansive taxonomy, or more commonly, from our curated packages, where we use a proven combination of segment categories that perform well for specific advertiser verticals: food and beverage, travel, app installs, etc.,” Madrid said. “Regardless of whether advertisers run programmatic or managed service campaigns, they can choose from several options for how to best align their brand with content and the consumer’s mindset.”
Emotion is a powerful signal, and emotional tone changes from scene to scene. Because each scene carries a unique mood and message, real-time analysis ensures ads match the current moment and are aligned with viewers’ emotional state.
Emotions also play a significant role in decision-making and ad success. According to research from Integral Ad Science, ads aligned with the consumer’s emotional state or surrounding content are up to 40% more memorable. Other studies show that more than 90% of purchasing decisions are driven by emotional responses.
In practice, emotions are more complex than just happy or sad — and savvy advertisers use these subtleties to their advantage across the funnel.
Consider this lower-funnel example, in which global agency PMG leveraged Wurl’s scene-level targeting to run emotionally targeted CTV ads on behalf of a quick-service restaurant (QSR) client. Through scene-level targeting, the ads were matched to content that evoked feelings of anticipation and joy to drive measurable sales results, validated by independent measurement partner InMarket.
“By optimizing delivery around those high-performing emotional signals, such as anticipation, the campaign drove a 40% lift in incremental restaurant visits and a 48% lift in incremental sales, making emotion-led placements the top-performing CTV tactic in the flight,” Madrid said. “It’s a clear example of how moment-level alignment increases attention — and attention translates directly into measurable business impact.”
As Madrid explained, driving outcomes and measuring performance in CTV has been a top-of-mind challenge for advertisers. Third-party validation shows that when ads align with what’s on screen, advertisers see benefits such as improved brand recall, engagement and purchase intent.
“Through working with various measurement partners like Kantar, Upwave, EDO and InMarket, what we’re really seeing is that targeting at the scene level improves effectiveness holistically — not just at one stage, but throughout the entire customer journey,” Madrid said. “At the top, we see lifts in brand awareness and favorability. Mid-funnel, stronger motivation and purchase intent. And at the lower funnel, measurable outcomes like incremental store visits and sales.
“When creative aligns with mindset and moment, the ad feels less disruptive and more relevant — and that drives performance across the funnel because those moments directly influence attention and impact.”
Scene-level targeting does not need to be used in a vacuum. It can be easily added to advertisers’ existing strategies, helping them reach their target audience in a CTV context that is relevant to their campaign and creative.
For instance, in the QSR campaign mentioned previously, Wurl ran a controlled CTV test designed to evaluate two targeting approaches: audience and regional targeting alone and audience and regional targeting layered with scene-level targeting. The agency tapped an independent measurement firm to validate results and provide a clear view into the incremental impact of each strategy.
The campaign analysis revealed that adding scene-level targeting nearly doubled the performance of audience and regional targeting alone. By combining geographic, audience and scene-level targeting, the campaign effectively delivered both relevance and reach.
“When done correctly, combining CTV targeting strategies is where precision really starts to take shape,” Madrid said. “Audience and demographic targeting have long been the norm, ensuring the right viewers are being reached. Scene-level contextual targeting ensures they are being reached during the right moments of their viewing session — in this case, following content that is both brand-suitable and safe. When those layers work together, advertisers don’t have to choose between scale and suitability. It’s a ‘yes, and.’”
To fully unlock the potential of CTV advertising, marketers need to adapt their strategies to the streaming landscape. The good news: adding scene-level targeting to existing CTV toolkits doesn’t have to be a heavy lift.
The easiest way to begin is by layering scene-level signals on top of existing audience and demographic targeting — enhancing relevance without sacrificing scale. This allows marketers to maintain reach while improving the context and impact of their messaging.
When evaluating partners, it’s important to prioritize solutions that deliver both precision and scale. Look for providers that offer high-quality, real-time signals and can seamlessly integrate into existing programmatic workflows — enabling activation without added operational complexity. Signal accuracy and ease of activation are critical, as these inputs ultimately determine campaign performance.
As the ecosystem evolves, advertisers will have greater flexibility in how they access and activate contextual data. New approaches are making it easier to pair premium streaming inventory with differentiated contextual solutions, giving marketers more choice without disrupting existing buying workflows. For instance, Wurl’s Content Intelligence Platform reflects this shift, enabling advertisers to access Wurl’s own scene-level targeting, as well as helping partners like KERV, Peer39 and IRIS.TV to scale their own precise and unique CTV targeting solutions. For marketers, that means greater choice, more relevant contextual signals and the flexibility to activate the solutions that best align with their campaign objectives.
This flexibility will become even more important as programmatic buying becomes more automated and AI-driven. In an environment driven by agentic workflows and automated decision-making, campaign performance will depend on the quality of the underlying contextual data.
“We hear about agentic workflows and AI-driven solutions being championed across the industry — how it will improve efficiency, efficacy, creative and ultimately provide cost savings across organizations of all sizes. All of these promises translate into improved performance,” Madrid said. “As more investment flows into these agentic environments, we cannot ignore the fact that it’s the underlying data sources that underpin the success of automation and curation. Scene-level segments and real-time categorization support all of the above.”
results.summary:
Scene-level targeting allows CTV advertisers to align ad creative with the specific emotional tone and context of onscreen content, significantly improving viewer attention and campaign performance metrics.

### Key Points
- Scene-level targeting uses generative AI to analyze audio, visual, and dialogue cues in real time to categorize content before ad breaks.
- Research indicates that ads matched to the emotional context of a scene see a 2.4x increase in viewer attention.
- The strategy improves brand safety by allowing advertisers to target specific, appropriate moments within genres like news that were previously excluded.
- A QSR campaign using scene-level targeting achieved a 40% lift in incremental restaurant visits and a 48% increase in sales.
- This approach functions without cookies or personal identifiers, ensuring compliance with privacy regulations like the Video Privacy Protection Act.

### Why it Matters
By moving beyond broad audience demographics to granular, moment-based targeting, brands can reduce ad dissonance and increase consumer engagement across the entire marketing funnel. This shift enables publishers to monetize inventory more effectively while providing advertisers with a scalable, privacy-compliant method to maximize the impact of their CTV investments.

results.title: Burrage receives support after online death threats
results.author: Jonathan Jurejko
results.content:
- Published
Britain's Jodie Burrage has been receiving support from WTA staff at an event in India after being sent death threats on social media.
Burrage, 27, was bombarded with abusive online messages when she was beaten in her first WTA Tour singles main-draw match in 16 months on Tuesday.
On Wednesday, she won in the last 16 of the Chennai Open doubles alongside Robin Montgomery of the United States.
"Protecting players and the wider tennis family from online threats and abuse is a key priority for the WTA," the governing body told BBC Sport.
"We have WTA staff on the ground in Chennai offering Jodie support, along with our wider player welfare and Threat Matrix team."
Burrage shared a story on her Instagram account that showed the direct messages she had been sent following a 3-6 6-3 7-5 loss to India's Vaishnavi Adkar.
"Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left," Burrage wrote.
Burrage tagged the WTA into the post, asking when action will be taken to combat abuse. Other players, including Germany's Eva Lys, showed solidarity with the former world number 85.
Is enough being done to protect players?
The WTA insists it is taking a "proactive approach" to protecting female players from abuse.
The Threat Matrix system, which uses artificial intelligence-led detection, can identify people behind the accounts that threaten players, enabling investigations to take place and potentially leading to legal action.
Female players were subjected to more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media last year, according to data from the service.
"Through Threat Matrix, a system we established in 2023, delivered by Signify Group alongside World Tennis, we identify, investigate and take action against those responsible," the WTA added.
"This includes reporting abusive content for removal, escalating serious cases to law enforcement and supporting action to prevent real-world harm.
"As much of the abuse players receive comes through direct messages, the WTA has offered Jodie additional support.
"These include a private channel to report abusive direct messages, and moderation that hides abusive comments on public channels before she sees them."
In 2024, a report from Signify found that angry gamblers were behind 48% of posts which were deemed to be abusive.
They were responsible for 42% of verified abuse in 2025 and 59% of cases of serious abuse.
The WTA is working with several gambling companies in a programme that flags abuse from gamblers in real time, allowing the operator to take direct action against those targeting athletes.
The company is then able to flag, restrict or suspend the account.
Mhairi Maclennan, chief executive of the Kyniska Advocacy, which supports female athletes, believes there is "still not enough being done" to protect athletes across the board.
"I'm afraid it is all too common for athletes who have public profiles to receive this type of abuse," she told BBC Radio 5 Live's Drive programme.
"Whether they have won or lost, a lot of the athletes we speak to report they have received abuse - whether death threats or rape threats - because of their public profile and because sports like tennis are tied to betting.
"Sports need a healthier relationship with betting agencies. Ultimately sports need money but we need to be looking at what betting is doing to individual athletes and looking after their welfare."
results.summary:
British tennis player Jodie Burrage is receiving support from the WTA after being targeted with death threats on social media following her recent singles match in Chennai, India.

### Key Points
- Jodie Burrage received abusive messages after losing her first WTA Tour singles match in 16 months to Vaishnavi Adkar.
- The WTA is providing support through its Threat Matrix team, which uses AI to identify and investigate online abusers.
- Data from Signify Group indicates that gamblers were responsible for 59% of serious abuse cases against athletes in 2025.
- The WTA has implemented private reporting channels and comment moderation tools to protect players from direct message harassment.
- The governing body collaborates with gambling companies to flag and suspend accounts that target athletes with real-time abuse.

### Why it Matters
This incident highlights the persistent challenge of online harassment in professional sports, particularly regarding the intersection of athlete welfare and the betting industry. As sports organizations increasingly rely on gambling partnerships, they face growing pressure to implement more effective safeguards against the rising volume of abuse directed at players.

results.title: Vercel rolls out new protection against stolen session cookie attacks
results.author: Bill Toulas
results.content:
Vercel is gradually rolling out Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) on its platform as a key defense against information stealer malware.
The new feature, announced by Vercel's CTO Malte Ubl on X, binds a login session to the user's device with a private key stored in a TPM, so even if the session cookie is stolen, it can't be reused on another device.
Vercel is a cloud platform developers use to deploy and host websites, web applications, and AI agents. The company also develops the popular Next.js web framework.
Its latest announcement concerns logins to Vercel's platform at vercel.com, where developers manage their projects and deployments.
"DBSC works by storing a private key in your device's TPM (the same device that the fingerprint sensor or similar biometric devices on your laptop or phone uses) and using that key to sign your cookie," explained Ubl.
"The private key can never be retrieved ever again. Not by us, not by you, not by the malware."
Vercel's DBSC rollout also complements Chrome's App-Bound Encryption, which makes it harder for infostealer malware to extract browser cookies. DBSC adds another layer of protection by preventing stolen session cookies from being reused on other devices.
DBSC currently works in Chrome on macOS and Windows, but the rollout is gradual to ensure edge cases involving OAuth apps are handled appropriately.
Separately, Vercel is rolling out a similar protective technology called DPoP for the Vercel CLI.
Security Review also lands
Earlier this week, Vercel launched Security Review in public beta for Pro and Enterprise teams, adding a feature to Vercel Agent that scans code changes on every push to connected GitHub repositories once enabled.
The new system uses code and team-defined policies to flag issues such as missing authorization checks and exposed secrets.
If permissions allow, the Vercel Agent can validate and commit fixes.
Vercel says Security Review scans will be free until November 10, 2026, while agent-generated fixes will be billed separately.
Ubl said that Vercel's security team shipped this new feature internally a couple of months back, and it has already proven its worth, so the platform decided to make it broadly available.
In April, Vercel suffered a security breach impacting a subset of customers, in which attackers gained access to its systems by compromising an employee's Google Workspace account at Context.ai.
Vercel said the attacker used that access to reach internal systems and view environment variables that hadn't been marked as sensitive.
A threat actor impersonating ShinyHunters attempted to sell the allegedly stolen source code, access keys, and database data.

results.summary:
Vercel is implementing Device Bound Session Credentials to prevent information-stealing malware from reusing stolen session cookies by binding user logins to specific hardware-based security keys on local devices.

### Key Points
- Vercel is rolling out Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) to bind login sessions to a device's Trusted Platform Module (TPM).
- The feature prevents stolen session cookies from being used on unauthorized devices, complementing Chrome’s existing App-Bound Encryption.
- DBSC is currently available for Chrome users on macOS and Windows, with a gradual rollout to manage OAuth compatibility.
- Vercel also introduced a Security Review feature in public beta that scans GitHub code pushes for authorization flaws and exposed secrets.
- Security Review scans will remain free for Pro and Enterprise teams until November 10, 2026, with automated fixes billed separately.

### Why it Matters
These security enhancements represent a proactive effort by Vercel to protect developer environments following a significant data breach earlier this year. By adopting hardware-backed authentication and automated code scanning, the platform aims to mitigate risks posed by sophisticated malware and unauthorized access to sensitive project data.

results.title: US markets rise as Democrats sweep midterm elections
results.author: Al Jazeera Staff
results.content:
US markets are trending upwards after Democrats swept the midterm elections, taking control of both the House and Senate on Tuesday.
The Nasdaq opened on Wednesday up 1 percent, the Dow Jones Industrial Average up 1.8 percent and the S&P 500 up 1.1 percent as markets opened at 9:30am ET (14:30GMT).
Retailers that rely on imports, such as Walmart and Target, are up 1.3 percent and 3.3 percent, respectively, amid possible changes in tariff policy.
Health insurance provider UnitedHealthcare is down 2.9 percent, while CVS Health is down 12 percent. However, Cigna went up 1.6 percent.
Investor sentiment was also buoyed by United States President Donald Trump’s social media post saying he would accept the results, easing political uncertainty and pressure on markets.
For companies involved in the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout, the outlook is different as the Democrats have been more critical of the sector.
Oracle and Nvidia both opened the day lower, although Alphabet, Google’s parent company, is on the upswing, up 3.5 percent at the opening bell.
“There is no way to sugarcoat that Democrats taking control, especially over the Senate, will create some major hurdles for AI and tech legislation in the Beltway over the next two years,” Dan Ives, managing partner of Yorkville Ives, said in a note on Wednesday.
“We estimate 10% of datacenters will not happen now,” Ives added in a post on X.
Democrats performed well in states where the AI buildout is pronounced, including Ohio, where Sherrod Brown flipped the Senate seat; Texas, where Democrats took a Senate seat with James Talarico; and the governor’s race, which Gina Hinojosa won, also flipping the seat.
Oil prices are also on the decline. The global benchmark Brent crude oil futures are down $3.20, or 3.09 percent, to $100.40 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate crude is down $3.01, or 3.13 percent, to $93.08.
While oil prices are reacting to the midterm results, investors are also watching to see whether the war with Iran and the one between Russia and Ukraine will end amid reports of talks, following the previous session, which saw oil prices hit their lowest levels in four weeks.
results.summary:
US markets trended upward on Wednesday following a Democratic sweep of the midterm elections, as investors reacted to shifting political control and potential changes in federal policy.

### Key Points
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.8 percent, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq gained 1.1 percent and 1 percent, respectively.
- Retailers Walmart and Target saw shares climb 1.3 percent and 3.3 percent amid expectations of potential shifts in national tariff policy.
- Healthcare stocks showed mixed results, with CVS Health dropping 12 percent and UnitedHealthcare falling 2.9 percent, while Cigna rose 1.6 percent.
- Tech companies faced volatility, as Oracle and Nvidia shares declined while Alphabet stock increased by 3.5 percent at the opening bell.
- Global oil prices dropped significantly, with Brent crude falling 3.09 percent to $100.40 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate declining 3.13 percent to $93.08.

### Why it Matters
The shift in legislative control creates significant uncertainty for the artificial intelligence sector, with analysts predicting potential delays in data center development due to increased regulatory scrutiny. Investors are now balancing these domestic political changes against cooling energy prices and ongoing geopolitical developments in Ukraine and Iran.
